A Kentucky funeral home that insists on embalming before a viewing is applying its own policy, not state law, and it must tell you so before charging the roughly $640 our Kentucky estimate shows. Kentucky's Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors (502-426-4589) takes it from there if it does not.

funeral-costs-louisiana.html.Is embalming legally required in Louisia:
Only after 30 hours without refrigeration. La. R.S. 37:848 requires a body held longer than 30 hours after death to be embalmed or kept continuously at 45°F or below; otherwise it must be buried or cremated within 30 hours. The Board's rule (51 La. Admin. Code Pt. XXVI, 103) also requires embalming or cremation before a body is moved out of Louisiana more than 24 hours after death, and it does not require embalming where religious practice forbids it.

For a body that stays in Louisiana and is refrigerated, the roughly $670 our Louisiana estimate puts on embalming is optional, and a funeral home needs your approval before it can charge it.
funeral-costs-louisiana.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Start with the price lists of three Louisiana funeral homes and compare direct cremation, from about $1,700 here, and immediate burial. The State Board of Embalmers and Funeral Directors (504-838-5109) can confirm that a provider is licensed.

Body donation can remove most of the cost. LSU Health New Orleans' Bureau of Anatomical Services arranges and pays transport for registered donors who die within 200 miles of New Orleans; the family pays the mileage beyond that. Registering requires a form signed before a notary and two witnesses, so it has to be done in advance.

funeral-costs-maryland.html.Is embalming legally required in Marylan:
No. Maryland goes further than most states: under Health-General § 5-513(d), a body may not be embalmed at all without the express permission of the person authorized to arrange disposition, or a court order. If an unembalmed body will be stored more than 48 hours, the funeral home or crematory must refrigerate it (§ 5-513(b)).

Embalming costs about $920 in Maryland on this page's estimate, above NFDA's 2023 national median of $845.
funeral-costs-maryland.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Compare the direct cremation lines from several Maryland funeral homes first; this site's estimate starts around $2,200. Maryland also requires express permission before embalming, so a low-cost provider should not be adding that charge unless you asked for it.

Maryland's State Anatomy Board runs a body donation program at no cost to the family when the donor dies in Maryland: it pays for transport, preparation and cremation. If the death happens in a neighboring state, the family pays to bring the body into Maryland and to file the death and cremation certificates.
funeral-costs-maryland.html.Where does Maryland rank nationally for:
Maryland's $9,200 traditional-funeral estimate is 11% above the $8,300 national median and ranks eighth highest among the 50 states on this site's estimates. It is above every neighboring state here: Delaware is $8,600, Pennsylvania $8,500 and Virginia $8,200.

The national $8,300 figure is NFDA's 2023 survey median; the state numbers are this site's estimates, not a separate survey. Maryland's direct cremation estimate is $2,200.

funeral-costs-massachusetts.html.Does Massachusetts require embalming?:
Not usually. Under 239 CMR 3.10, an unembalmed body that will be buried or cremated in Massachusetts within 50 hours of death must still be washed, disinfected and wrapped by a licensed embalmer. If disposition will take longer than 50 hours, the body must also be kept at 34 to 39°F; if that is not possible, it must be embalmed unless the family directs otherwise in writing.

A local board of health can order embalming in cases of advanced decomposition. At about $1,040 on our Massachusetts estimate, embalming here costs more than NFDA's 2023 national median of $845, so if you do not want it, give the written direction mentioned above.
funeral-costs-massachusetts.html.Where does Massachusetts rank nationally:
Massachusetts's $10,400 traditional-funeral estimate is 25% above the $8,300 national median and the fourth highest of the 50 states on this site's estimates, behind Hawaii, New York and California. It is also above NFDA's 2023 New England regional median of $8,985.

Direct cremation in Massachusetts is estimated at about $2,500, which ranks near the top as well. The national $8,300 figure is NFDA's survey median, while the state figures are this site's estimates.

funeral-costs-michigan.html.Is embalming legally required in Michiga:
Only in narrow cases. Michigan's transport rules (Mich. Admin. Code R 325.1 and 325.2) require embalming for bodies of people who died of certain diseases, such as diphtheria or plague, and for any body shipped by common carrier that cannot reach its destination within 48 hours of death. If family members dispute disposition and refrigeration is not available, the funeral home may embalm while the court decides (MCL 700.3207).

Otherwise it is optional, and declining it takes about $720 off a Michigan bill on this page's estimate.
funeral-costs-michigan.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Ask several Michigan funeral homes for their General Price Lists and compare the direct cremation line, which starts around $1,700 here. Compare the basic services fee too, since every arrangement carries it.

The University of Michigan Medical School's Anatomical Donations Program (734-764-4359) accepts whole-body donors. A funeral home has to be hired to deliver the body to Ann Arbor, and distance or transport cost can rule a donation out, but there is an expense-free route for pre-registered donors who die as Michigan Medicine inpatients. Remains are cremated, and the ashes are returned if the family asked in writing.

funeral-costs-mississippi.html.Is embalming legally required in Mississ:
No. The Health Department's rules say Mississippi does not require embalming, caskets or vaults, with one exception (15 Miss. Admin. Code Pt. 5, R. 4.6.3): a body must be buried or cremated within 48 hours of death unless it is embalmed or refrigerated, and a body transported that cannot reach its destination within 24 hours must be embalmed or refrigerated.

Embalming costs about $590 in Mississippi on this page's estimate, below NFDA's 2023 national median of $845.
funeral-costs-mississippi.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Compare direct cremation, from about $1,400 here, on at least three Mississippi price lists, and ask about immediate burial if cremation is not an option for your family.

The University of Mississippi Medical Center's Anatomical Gift Program ordinarily costs the family nothing beyond death certificate copies: for an accepted donor who dies in Mississippi it covers removal from anywhere in the state, preparation, cremation and return of the ashes. If UMMC declines the donation at the time of death, the family has to arrange and pay for a funeral, so keep a backup price list.

funeral-costs-missouri.html.Does Missouri require embalming?:
No. Under 20 CSR 2120-2.070, a Missouri funeral home may not hold an unembalmed body longer than 24 hours unless it is refrigerated at 40°F or below or sealed in an airtight casket. The same rule requires written authorization to embalm, which the deceased can give in advance, including in a preneed contract.

A county coroner can order embalming when no family can be found within six hours (RSMo § 58.375), and the family pays later. Because Missouri requires written authorization, a charge of about $680 (our Missouri estimate) should not appear on a bill unless someone signed for it or the coroner ordered it.

funeral-costs-nevada.html.Does Nevada require embalming?:
No. NRS 451.065 bars crematories, funeral homes and cemeteries from requiring embalming before burial, cremation or transport. Only the State Board of Health can require it to protect the public, and the Funeral and Cemetery Services Board can approve embalming after a body has been held 72 hours if no family member can be reached.

Outside those cases it is the family's call, and the roughly $800 Nevada figure on this page can stay off the bill. Questions about an unapproved charge go to that same board at 775-825-5535.
funeral-costs-nevada.html.How can I find affordable funeral homes: Ask each home what it charges for transport from the place of death. Request each General Price List, compare direct cremation and immediate burial lines, and check licenses with the Funeral and Cemetery Services Board.
funeral-costs-nevada.html.What is the average price of a funeral i: On our 2026 figures a Nevada funeral with viewing and burial averages $8,000, a funeral with cremation $6,200, and direct cremation starts near $1,800. Burial adds roughly $3,800 for the plot and cemetery charges. These are estimates anchored to the $8,300 NFDA national median, not quotes; Las Vegas and Reno homes publish General Price Lists you can compare.
funeral-costs-nevada.html.Is cremation cheaper than burial in Neva: Yes, by a wide margin. Direct cremation at about $1,800 is roughly $6,200 under an $8,000 traditional funeral, and close to $10,000 under it once about $3,800 in cemetery costs is included. Nevada has no waiting period before cremation, but the crematory needs a signed death certificate and written authorization (NRS 451.660).
funeral-costs-nevada.html.How do I keep funeral costs down in Neva: Compare at least three General Price Lists, take apart any package so you pay only for what you want, and choose direct cremation (about $1,800) if cost comes first. Nevada law lets you refuse embalming (NRS 451.065). Veterans can be buried at the Fernley or Boulder City state veterans cemetery, and families without means can ask the county about help under NRS 428.090.
funeral-costs-nevada.html.Is Nevada cheaper or more expensive than: Close to average. The $8,000 Nevada estimate is about 4% below the $8,300 national median for a funeral with viewing and burial, and the $6,200 cremation-funeral figure is near the $6,280 national cremation median (NFDA 2023). Individual homes vary, so collect several price lists.

funeral-costs-new-hampshire.html.Does New Hampshire require embalming?:
No. RSA 325:40-b requires that if disposition has not happened within 48 hours after the funeral home takes custody, the body be embalmed, kept below 40°F, or sealed in a leak-proof container. With refrigeration, embalming remains your choice.

New Hampshire funeral homes are licensed through the Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (603-271-2152), which is also where to report a charge for embalming you did not approve; this page estimates that charge at about $880 in New Hampshire.
funeral-costs-new-hampshire.html.Is cremation cheaper than burial in New: Yes, by a wide margin. Direct cremation at about $2,100 is roughly $6,700 below the $8,800 traditional New Hampshire funeral, and the gap grows to about $11,100 once a $4,400 plot and its cemetery fees are counted. A memorial service can still be held after cremation.
funeral-costs-new-hampshire.html.How can I find affordable funeral homes: Phone several New Hampshire homes and ask for their prices; the FTC Funeral Rule requires them to answer by phone. If the person received public assistance, also call the town welfare officer, since RSA 165:3 may cover a basic burial or cremation. You may supply your own casket or urn without paying a handling fee.

funeral-costs-new-jersey.html.Is embalming legally required in New Jer:
Not in New Jersey, as long as the body is kept cold. N.J.A.C. 8:9-1.1 does not allow a body to remain unburied or uncremated in New Jersey longer than 48 hours unless it is embalmed or kept at 45°F or below. It also bars bringing an unembalmed body into the state more than 48 hours after death, except under an emergency waiver from the Commissioner of Health.

For an in-state funeral with refrigeration, the roughly $1,020 that embalming adds on our New Jersey estimate is a choice, and a disputed charge can be raised with the State Board of Mortuary Science through the Division of Consumer Affairs (973-504-6425).
funeral-costs-new-jersey.html.What does the FTC Funeral Rule mean for:
The federal Rule gives you an itemized General Price List, prices by phone and the right to buy only what you choose. New Jersey writes much of the same into its own rules: funeral homes must give you a general price list, a casket price list and an outer burial container price list (N.J.A.C. 13:36-9.7), and a signed Statement of Funeral Goods and Services Selected that itemizes each charge (N.J.A.C. 13:36-1.9).

For a prepaid funeral, New Jersey requires the money to go into a funeral trust or a funeral insurance policy, and the price lists and statement must be given at the time of the sale (N.J.A.C. 13:36-11.2).

funeral-costs-oklahoma.html.Is embalming legally required in Oklahom:
Not in Oklahoma when the body is refrigerated instead, though the time limits are short. The Funeral Board's rule (Okla. Admin. Code 235:10-11-1) requires an unembalmed body to be buried or cremated within 24 hours of death unless it is kept at 40°F or less, and once it leaves refrigeration it must be embalmed or disposed of within eight hours. The rule also bars public viewing of an unembalmed body more than 24 hours after death.

So a viewing held more than a day after death means paying for embalming, about $610 on our Oklahoma estimate, while direct cremation or a prompt burial does not. The Oklahoma Funeral Board (405-522-1790) licenses the homes that charge for it.
funeral-costs-oklahoma.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Request price lists from three Oklahoma funeral homes and compare direct cremation, from about $1,400 here, line by line.

The OU Health Sciences Center's Willed Body Program, overseen by the State Anatomical Board, accepts whole-body donations for medical teaching. After study, the body is cremated and the ashes can be returned to the family, scattered on university property, or included in a group interment. Ask the program about any transport costs before registering.

funeral-costs-oregon.html.Does Oregon require embalming?:
No. Under OAR 830-030-0010, a body held longer than 24 hours must be embalmed or refrigerated at 36°F or less, and embalming requires permission from the person with the right to control disposition. All remains must reach final disposition within 20 days of a funeral home taking custody, unless the Board is notified.

That 20-day limit, not an embalming rule, sets the timetable, and embalming (about $820 on this page's Oregon estimate) is needed only if you want it. Oregon's Mortuary and Cemetery Board, at 971-673-1500, licenses funeral homes and cemeteries alike and hears complaints about both.

funeral-costs-pennsylvania.html.Does Pennsylvania require embalming?:
No. Under 49 Pa. Code § 13.201, a body held more than 24 hours after death must be embalmed, sealed in a container, or refrigerated at 35 to 40°F, unless that conflicts with religious belief or a medical examination. Once out of refrigeration, it must be buried, cremated or entombed within five hours, and an unembalmed body refrigerated longer than 36 hours generally should not be publicly viewed.

Those timing rules make the viewing the deciding question: without one, the roughly $850 embalming charge on our Pennsylvania estimate can be left off. An unapproved charge can be reported to the State Board of Funeral Directors at 1-833-367-2762.
funeral-costs-pennsylvania.html.Where does Pennsylvania rank nationally:
Pennsylvania's $8,500 estimate for a traditional funeral is close to the $8,300 national median and ties with Illinois and Vermont for 13th highest of the 50 states on this site's estimates. Its neighbors New Jersey ($10,200), New York ($10,800) and Maryland ($9,200) all come in higher.

Direct cremation in Pennsylvania is estimated at about $2,000. The national $8,300 figure is NFDA's 2023 survey median; the state numbers are this site's estimates, so use them to compare states rather than to predict a single bill.

funeral-costs-rhode-island.html.Does Rhode Island require embalming?:
Only in limited cases. The Department of Health's rule (216-RICR-40-05-25.5.6) bars holding a body more than 48 hours without embalming or refrigeration, and a body sent by common carrier must be embalmed or, if that is not possible, sealed in a strong outer case.

Rhode Island's Board of Funeral Directing/Embalming, part of the Department of Health (401-222-4998), licenses the people who perform it; on this page's Rhode Island estimate, embalming runs about $900 when a family chooses it.

funeral-costs-south-carolina.html.Does South Carolina require embalming?:
No. The Board of Funeral Service says South Carolina law does not require embalming, that funeral homes may not say otherwise, and that it is not needed for cremation, though a family may want it for a viewing. Under the Board's crematory regulations (S.C. Code Regs. ch. 57), a crematory that refrigerates bodies it will hold 24 hours or more must use a unit that keeps 40°F when full.

None of that requires embalming for a prompt funeral, so the roughly $670 our South Carolina estimate shows for it is optional; the State Board of Funeral Service (803-896-4429) is where to take a dispute over the charge.

funeral-costs-tennessee.html.Is embalming legally required in Tenness:
No. Tennessee has no statute requiring embalming. The related rule is for crematories: an unembalmed body held eight hours or longer must be refrigerated until cremation (Tenn. Code Ann. 62-5-507).

This page's Tennessee estimate puts embalming at about $670. If it shows up on a bill without your approval, call the Board of Funeral Directors and Embalmers at 615-741-5062.
funeral-costs-tennessee.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Ask at least three Tennessee funeral homes for their price lists and compare direct cremation, from about $1,600 here. Ask whether the price includes every permit and the death certificate copies, since some homes list those separately.

Body donation to the University of Tennessee's Forensic Anthropology Center is free, and the center transports the body at no cost from a hospital, funeral home or medical examiner's office within 100 miles of Knoxville. From a home, hospice or nursing home, or from farther away, the family pays a funeral home for that step.

funeral-costs-texas.html.Does Texas require embalming?:
No. The Texas Funeral Service Commission's consumer guide says state law does not require embalming. Under 25 TAC § 181.4, a body not buried or cremated within 24 hours must be refrigerated at 34 to 40°F, embalmed, or sealed in a container, and Commission rules (22 TAC 203.32–203.33) require written or documented permission before any embalming.

Airlines and other common carriers usually require it, so ask about it if the body will be flown. For a Texas funeral without air travel, refrigeration satisfies the 24-hour rule and saves the roughly $720 this page estimates for embalming.

funeral-costs-washington.html.Is embalming legally required in Washing:
No. Under RCW 18.39.215, a funeral home must refrigerate or embalm a body as soon as it receives it, and must tell the family that state law does not require embalming except under certain Board of Health conditions. Embalming also requires authorization from the person with the right to control disposition.

Without that authorization a Washington funeral home has no basis to bill the roughly $880 this page estimates for embalming, and the Department of Licensing (360-664-1555), which licenses funeral homes, takes complaints about such charges.
funeral-costs-washington.html.Where do I look for low-cost funeral pro:
Compare direct cremation, from about $2,100 here, on several Washington price lists, and ask whether the provider also offers natural organic reduction or alkaline hydrolysis, both legal in Washington.

When the University of Washington's Willed Body Program accepts a donor, it pays for transport and cremation and then either mails the ashes to a named recipient or buries them in its communal site at Evergreen-Washelli; the family pays only for any plot it chooses. Families who need a fallback should still get one funeral home's direct cremation price in case the program cannot accept the body.

funeral-flowers-guide.html.Is it acceptable to ask for donations in:
Yes. An "in lieu of flowers" line in the obituary naming one charity is common and widely understood. Give the charity's exact name and, if it has several branches, which one, so gifts reach the right place, and ask the charity whether it will send the family a list of donors so thank-you notes can go out.

A gift to a qualified charity can be deductible for donors who itemize, but a gift sent to the family to help with the funeral is not (IRS Publication 526). Donors can check a charity's status on the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search, and a gift of $250 or more needs a written acknowledgment from the charity.
funeral-flowers-guide.html.Who pays for the casket spray?:
Usually the immediate family: the spouse or the children, and sometimes the siblings, choose and pay for it, often splitting the cost among themselves (MSU Extension, Sympathy Floral Design Manual). Friends, coworkers and organizations more often send standing sprays, wreaths or plants instead.

Decide early which relative is placing the order, so the funeral home and the family do not each order a spray for the same casket.

funeral-planning-for-parents.html.When should I talk to my parents about f:
While they are healthy and there is no urgency. A friend's funeral or a will update is a natural opening. Waiting has a practical cost: a will, a power of attorney and a health care proxy can only be signed while a parent still understands what they are signing, and those are the papers this guide asks you to find.

Many parents have not done this yet. In NFDA's 2025 Consumer Awareness and Preferences Study, 19.4% of respondents said they had both pre-planned and prepaid their funeral, so most families still have the conversation ahead of them. If a parent does buy a prepaid plan, keep a copy of the contract with the other papers.

hindu-funeral-costs.html.What makes a Hindu funeral different fro:
The rites continue well after the cremation. In the North American practice set out by the Hindu Mandir Executives' Conference, the ashes are collected the day after cremation (sanchayana), a lamp is kept lit at home, and a memorial puja, bhajan or talk is held on the 4th, 10th or 13th day at a mandir, at home or at a community center, often followed by a meal.

The 13-day mourning period ends with a purification ceremony (punyahavachanam) on the 13th day. Customs vary by region and family, and the same guide advises families to follow their elders and priest. Each of those gatherings can add costs a secular funeral does not have, which is why this page's table lists the 13th day ceremony separately.

jewish-funeral-costs.html.What makes a Jewish funeral different fr:
The chevra kadisha (burial society) performs tahara, the ritual washing and dressing in plain white shrouds, and a shomer may stay with the body until the funeral. Embalming is generally avoided; it is allowed when the body must travel a long way or the law requires it. Burial ideally takes place within 24 hours, in a plain wooden casket (My Jewish Learning).

After burial, close relatives sit shiva for seven days, usually at home, and receive visitors. Sheloshim, a lighter mourning period, runs through the 30th day after the burial. Those days of hosting are why this page's table includes shiva expenses as a separate row.

mormon-funeral-costs.html.What makes a LDS / Mormon funeral differ:
A Latter-day Saint funeral is usually a church meeting held in the ward meetinghouse and conducted under the direction of the bishop, and the Church does not charge for using the building. The General Handbook (section 38.5.8) asks that the service be simple and centered on the gospel, with talks and music rather than a long program of eulogies.

Endowed members are typically dressed in temple clothing, which the family or the ward's Relief Society helps arrange, and the grave is often dedicated by a Melchizedek Priesthood holder at the cemetery. Funeral home fees, the casket and the cemetery are still paid separately, so the savings come mainly from the venue and volunteer help.

probate-process-costs.html.Does a mortgage reduce California probat:
No. California's statutory fee base is the appraised value of estate property without subtracting mortgages or other debts (Cal. Prob. Code § 10810; Alameda County Superior Court). Take an estate whose only asset is a $750,000 house with a $500,000 mortgage: the fee base is $750,000, so the attorney's statutory fee is $18,000 (4,000 + 3,000 + 11,000), and the personal representative may claim another $18,000 under § 10800.

If the fee were figured on the $250,000 of equity instead, each fee would be $8,000 (4,000 + 3,000 + 1,000). The gap matters most for a heavily mortgaged home; a house retitled into a funded living trust stays out of the probate estate, as described above. A personal representative can also negotiate a lower fee than the statutory amount.

funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.What rights do New Mexico families have: The FTC Funeral Rule gives you an itemized price list, prices over the phone, and the right to bring a casket or urn bought elsewhere with no handling fee. New Mexico adds no funeral-director requirement, so you can pick individual services. The Board of Funeral Services (505-476-4622) takes complaints when a home breaks those rules.
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.What is the best way to find a cheap fun: Phone several homes in your area, ask each for its direct cremation and immediate burial prices, and request the General Price List in writing. Check the license with the Board of Funeral Services before paying a deposit.
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.How much does a funeral cost in New Mexi: Our New Mexico estimate is $6,400 for a traditional funeral with burial, $5,200 for a funeral followed by cremation and about $1,500 for direct cremation, with a plot adding roughly $2,800. Homes in Albuquerque, Las Cruces and smaller towns price differently, so the General Price Lists of two or three nearby homes will tell you more than any average.
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.How much cheaper is cremation than buria: About $4,900 before the cemetery is counted: direct cremation runs near $1,500 against a $6,400 traditional funeral. Add the $2,800 plot estimate and the gap passes $7,000. Remember that cremation in New Mexico waits for the medical investigator's permit (NMSA 61-32-19).
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.How can I save on funeral costs in New M: Compare written price lists before agreeing to anything, and buy only the items you want, since New Mexico does not make you hire a director for every step. A memorial after direct cremation (about $1,500) avoids embalming and viewing. For a veteran, a national or state veterans cemetery removes the plot cost, and a family with no estate should ask the county about its $1,000 help.
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.Do I have to embalm a loved one in New M: Usually not. Under the FTC Funeral Rule a home may not tell you embalming is legally required when it is not, and its price list has to say so. If a New Mexico home insists, ask it to name the statute or cemetery rule. Declining embalming keeps the $640 average charge in our table off the bill, though a public viewing may not be possible without it.
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.Is New Mexico cheaper or more expensive: Cheaper. The $6,400 New Mexico estimate for a traditional funeral is about 23% under the $8,300 national median for a funeral with viewing and burial (NFDA 2023).
funeral-costs-new-mexico.html.What is the cheapest funeral option in N: Direct cremation, from roughly $1,500, costs the least in New Mexico because there is no viewing, ceremony or embalming. Direct burial is the next step up at about $3,200, but the family still needs a grave, and the $2,800 plot estimate applies unless the person is eligible for a veterans cemetery.

funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.What rights do South Dakota families hav: Under the FTC Funeral Rule a South Dakota home must hand you an itemized General Price List, give prices by phone, and accept a casket or urn you bought elsewhere without charging extra. No state law forces you to use a funeral director for every step. Complaints go to the State Board of Funeral Service at 605-642-1600.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.What is the best way to find a cheap fun: Ring three homes, the closest plus two in neighboring towns, and ask each for the same three prices: direct cremation, immediate burial and a memorial without a viewing. Ask too what they charge to collect the body from the place of death. Before paying a deposit, the State Board of Funeral Service at 605-642-1600 can confirm the license.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.How much does a funeral cost in South Da: We estimate $6,400 for a traditional South Dakota funeral with burial and $5,200 for a funeral with cremation, while direct cremation starts near $1,500. A cemetery plot is extra, about $2,800 on our figures. Ask homes in Sioux Falls, Rapid City or your own county for their price lists, since individual homes can be well above or below these numbers.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.How much cheaper is cremation than buria: Direct cremation, at roughly $1,500, is about $4,900 below a $6,400 traditional funeral in South Dakota, and the difference grows once a plot near $2,800 is bought. The state's 24-hour wait before cremation (SDCL 34-26A-13.1) rarely adds cost, but ask about refrigeration.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.How can I save on funeral costs in South: Get each home's price list, choose only the services you want, and consider direct cremation with a later memorial. Eligible veterans can be buried at Black Hills National Cemetery or a state or tribal veterans cemetery instead of a private plot. County poor relief exists for those without funds, but it is repaid through a lien on the estate.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.Do I have to embalm a loved one in South: South Dakota families can normally say no. Federal rules forbid a funeral home to present embalming as a legal must when no law calls for it, and the General Price List has to carry a written notice to that effect. A home that wants it for a public viewing can say so, but that is its policy, not the state's. Leaving it out drops the $640 average line in our table.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.Is South Dakota cheaper or more expensiv: Below average. Our $6,400 South Dakota traditional-funeral figure is roughly 23% less than the $8,300 national median reported by the NFDA for 2023.
funeral-costs-south-dakota.html.What is the cheapest funeral option in S: The lowest South Dakota price is for direct cremation, around $1,500, which can happen once the 24-hour wait has passed. Direct burial is the next step up at about $3,200; it skips the service and embalming, yet the plot, about $2,800 on our figures, is a separate cost.

funeral-costs-montana.html.What are my consumer rights at Montana f: The FTC Funeral Rule requires a Montana home to give you an itemized price list in person, quote prices by phone, and accept a casket or urn from another seller with no handling fee. Montana law does not require you to hire a funeral director. The Department of Labor and Industry (406-841-2359) takes complaints.
funeral-costs-montana.html.What is the best way to find a cheap fun: Price shopping by phone is allowed and homes must answer. Line up quotes for direct cremation and immediate burial from more than one community, and check whether removal from the place of death and mileage are in the quote. The Department of Labor and Industry confirms licenses.
funeral-costs-montana.html.What does a typical Montana funeral cost: Our 2026 Montana estimate is $7,100 for a traditional funeral with burial, $5,600 for a funeral with cremation and from about $1,600 for direct cremation, plus roughly $3,200 for a plot. Prices in Billings, Missoula and small towns differ, so ask nearby homes for their General Price Lists.
funeral-costs-montana.html.How much cheaper is cremation than buria: Direct cremation near $1,600 is about $5,500 less than a $7,100 traditional funeral in Montana, and the gap widens past $8,000 once a $3,200 plot is added. Montana requires 24 hours between death and cremation (MCA 37-19-705).
funeral-costs-montana.html.What is the best way to reduce funeral e: Ask for every home's price list and buy only the parts you need, since Montana does not require a funeral director. Direct cremation from about $1,600 with a later memorial is the lowest-cost route. A veteran can be buried at Yellowstone National Cemetery or one of the state veterans cemeteries, and some counties offer indigent funeral help under MCA 53-3-116.
funeral-costs-montana.html.Do I have to embalm a loved one in Monta: In most Montana cases, no. Embalming is an item you may decline, and the FTC requires the home's printed price list to tell you it is optional apart from special cases. Some homes ask for it before an open-casket viewing; a closed casket, a quick burial or direct cremation avoid the question. That keeps the $710 average off the bill.
funeral-costs-montana.html.How do funeral costs in Montana compare: Montana sits below the middle. Our $7,100 traditional-funeral estimate is about 14% under the $8,300 national median (NFDA 2023); see the national cost index for every state's figure.

funeral-costs-wisconsin.html.Is cremation cheaper than burial in Wisc: It is. A Wisconsin direct cremation near $1,700 costs about $5,500 less than the $7,200 traditional funeral, and close to $8,900 less after about $3,400 in cemetery costs. WFCAP can also put up to $1,000 toward crematory or cemetery charges for eligible families.
funeral-costs-wisconsin.html.Does Wisconsin require embalming?: Not in most cases. Wisconsin law does not make embalming routine, and the FTC Funeral Rule forbids a home from saying it is legally required unless it can cite the specific law. If there will be no public viewing, ask about refrigeration instead.
funeral-costs-wisconsin.html.How can I find affordable funeral homes: Ask three Wisconsin homes for General Price Lists and compare their direct cremation and immediate burial lines. Wisconsin's ban on solicitation (Wis. Stat. §445.12) means no one should pressure you into a choice, and the FTC Funeral Rule lets you bring a casket or urn from elsewhere without a fee.
funeral-costs-wisconsin.html.What does a typical Wisconsin funeral co: Our 2026 estimate for a traditional Wisconsin funeral is about $7,200, which is 13% under the $8,300 national median. A funeral with cremation is nearer $5,800 and direct cremation starts around $1,700, while a cemetery plot adds about $3,400. WFCAP can help eligible families, but only if the total bill stays within its limits, so collect quotes from more than one Wisconsin home before you sign.
funeral-costs-wisconsin.html.What is the least expensive way to handl: Direct cremation, at about $1,700 in Wisconsin, covers only transport, the cremation after the state's 48-hour wait, and the return of the ashes. For a burial, direct burial with no viewing or ceremony is the lowest-cost choice at around $3,600 before cemetery fees.
